title: PhD in Pangenomics of Wild Fisheries Species at Earlham Institute, UK

organization.name: Earlham Institute
organization.about: Earlham Institute is a life sciences research institute based at Norwich Research Park in England. Its research focuses on genomics and computational biology, using experimental and analytical approaches to understand living systems. The institute supports scientific collaboration, specialist technology and researcher training, connecting biological data with questions across diverse organisms.

intro: Earlham Institute is advertising an ARIES doctorate on genomic variation and population structure in Atlantic bluefin tuna and Atlantic herring. The project involves CEFAS researchers.
description:
Research Summary

Earlham Institute is advertising an ARIES doctorate on genomic variation and population structure in Atlantic bluefin tuna and Atlantic herring.

The project involves CEFAS researchers.

Official Project Title

Pangenomes and population genomics of wild fisheries species

Research Focus and Methods

Use long-read sequencing and pangenomes to investigate genetic diversity, structural variation and demographic history. The work connects genomic evidence with sustainable management of commercially harvested fish populations.

Research Training and Development

Training covers bioinformatics, population genetics and evidence relevant to fisheries policy.

Use the ARIES route linked from the Earlham advert. Do not use an Essex-specific submission email for this Earlham project. Consult the registering university’s current checklist.
